Calculate ∫5xsin⁡(x)dx.

a
cos⁡5x+xsin⁡5x+C
b
−5xsin⁡x+cos⁡x+C

−5xcos⁡x+5sin⁡x+C

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=5x and dv=sin(x) dx gives du=5 dx and v=-cos(x). Thus the integral is -5x cos(x)+5 sin(x)+C, which is option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 5\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 5\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)]+[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}-0]+[0-1] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)]+[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}-0]+[0-1] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=x and dv=cos(5x) dx gives v=sin(5x)/5. Therefore the integral is x sin(5x)/5−∫sin(5x)/5 dx=x sin(5x)/5+cos(5x)/25+C, matching option c.

after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x))-\int (-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)}{4}+\frac{1}{4}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & ={-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)}{4}|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)}{4}|}_{0}^{\pi }+{\frac{1}{16}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =[-\frac{\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(4\pi )}{4}+\frac{0\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot 0)}{4}] \\  & +\frac{1}{16}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0)] \\  & =(-\frac{\pi }{4}+0)+\frac{1}{16}(0-0) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}-\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{3}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & +\frac{1}{9}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{\pi }{2}-0)+\frac{1}{9}(0-1) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}-\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}

content.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}-\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{3}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & +\frac{1}{9}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{\pi }{2}-0)+\frac{1}{9}(0-1) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}-\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
